sub_graphs.title: EIP-4444: Client Synchronization State Transitions
sub_graphs.description: Models the state transitions for client synchronization under the bounded historical data regime

nodes.label: Client Uninitialized
nodes.description: New execution client has no blockchain state and needs to synchronize

nodes.label: Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint Received
nodes.description: Client has received a valid weak subjectivity checkpoint as bootstrap point

nodes.label: Validate Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint
nodes.description: Verify that the weak subjectivity checkpoint is valid and within acceptable time bounds

nodes.label: Checkpoint Validated
nodes.description: Weak subjectivity checkpoint has been verified as valid

nodes.label: Synchronize From Checkpoint
nodes.description: Begin synchronizing chain state from the validated checkpoint rather than genesis

nodes.label: Client Synchronized
nodes.description: Client has synchronized to current chain head from checkpoint

nodes.label: Checkpoint Invalid
nodes.description: Weak subjectivity checkpoint failed validation - client cannot safely sync

edges.label: Node operator provides weak subjectivity checkpoint

sub_graphs.title: EIP-4444: Historical Data Pruning State Machine
sub_graphs.description: Models the state transitions for historical data retention and pruning

nodes.label: Block Received
nodes.description: New block data received and stored locally

nodes.label: Store Block Data
nodes.description: Persist block header, body, and receipts to local storage

nodes.label: Data Within Retention Window
nodes.description: Block data is younger than HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS (82,125 epochs / ~1 year)

nodes.label: Check Data Age
nodes.description: Evaluate whether block data exceeds HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS threshold

nodes.label: Data Exceeds Retention Window
nodes.description: Block data is older than HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS and eligible for pruning

nodes.label: Prune Historical Data
nodes.description: Remove headers, block bodies, and receipts older than retention threshold

nodes.label: Historical Data Pruned
nodes.description: Old block data has been removed from local storage

external_entities.name: Peer Node
external_entities.description: Other execution client in the P2P network providing block data

sub_graphs.title: EIP-4444: P2P Data Serving Protocol Changes

nodes.label: Data Request Received

nodes.label: Evaluate Requested Data Age
nodes.description: Determine if requested data is within the serving window (HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS)

nodes.label: Request Within Serving Window
nodes.description: Requested data is recent enough to serve

nodes.label: Request Exceeds Serving Window
nodes.description: Requested data is older than HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS - SHOULD NOT serve

nodes.label: Serve Requested Data
nodes.description: Retrieve and transmit the requested block data to the peer

nodes.label: Decline Historical Data Request
nodes.description: Refuse to serve data older than the retention threshold

nodes.label: Data Served to Peer
nodes.description: Requested data successfully transmitted to requesting peer

nodes.label: Request Declined
nodes.description: Historical data request was refused due to age

nodes.label: External Data Validated
nodes.description: Historical data verified as authentic

ambiguities.text: Clients SHOULD NOT serve headers, block bodies, and receipts that are older than HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume SHOULD NOT as a soft requirement - clients MAY still serve old data but are not obligated. For security modeling, assume most clients will NOT serve old data after adoption.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define how to validate historical data obtained from out-of-band sources
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume validation requires checking data against known state roots or accumulator proofs. This is a critical security gap to address.

ambiguities.text: The weak subjectivity period must never exceed the history prune epoch threshold - relationship not precisely defined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume that HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS (82,125 epochs) must always be greater than the weak subjectivity period to ensure checkpoint data is available.

implicit_assumptions.description: Node operators are assumed to provide valid weak subjectivity checkpoints to their clients
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious or compromised checkpoint could lead to client syncing to an invalid chain state, enabling long-range attacks

implicit_assumptions.description: Out-of-band historical data sources (IPFS, Portal Network, indexers) will remain available and provide authentic data
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Historical data could become unavailable or corrupted, breaking dApps dependent on old blockchain data

implicit_assumptions.description: Organizations will voluntarily maintain and distribute historical blockchain data via alternative channels
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Historical data centralization risk - few entities controlling access to old blockchain data

implicit_assumptions.description: External historical data providers (The Graph, indexing services) can be trusted to serve authentic data
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Centralized data providers could serve falsified historical data to dependent applications
